name: fade
description: An edge fade — the gradient that dissolves overflowing content into the ground it sits on, signalling continuation: under a pinned header, above a composer bar, at the cut of a truncated preview. One aria-hidden span, absolutely pinned to one edge of the caller's clipping container, painting a perceptual ramp (fade-ramp: a Gaussian penumbra with a dark-scheme correction) in the container's own bg role, so there is no start line or stripe for the eye to catch. side (top/bottom/left/right), size (24/48/96 on the spacing scale) and ground (base/surface/elevated/sunken, or affix under a translucent pinned bar, where the ramp ends at the bar's own alpha) are the parameters. isVisible gates it by opacity on the motion tokens; scrollContainer binds it to a scroller, easing it out over the last band-depth of scroll instead of switching off at the end and insetting it off a classic scrollbar. It is paint, never a participant: pointer-events none, no children, no interactive targets in the band, and every faded region pairs with a caller-composed route to the full content. fadeMask is the ground-agnostic complement for containers whose ground is not a role.
